frequency_question: How often does a central bank raise the countercyclical capital buffer above zero within a defined short-term window given prevailing systemic risk indicator signals?
membership_rule: Includes all instances where a central bank actively maintained a 0% countercyclical capital buffer and evaluated or executed an increase during a normalization cycle; excludes jurisdictions where the buffer was already structurally positive.

cases.name: Reserve Bank of New Zealand CCyB increase

provenance_note: claimed 0 hits but 2 of 4 cases are marked hit; rate recomputed from the cases
coverage_note: 4 instances enumerated for the specific US institutional context; broader international analogues show rare upward movements from 0% outside of explicit post-crisis macroprudential build-up phases.
known_gaps: Strictly limited to the historical reluctance of the U.S. Federal Reserve to deploy the CCyB above 0% since its inception.
skeleton: Total policy evaluation windows for the Federal Reserve since the establishment of the CCyB framework where the buffer sat at 0%
multiplier: 4 major evaluation cycles observed with zero upward adjustments executed from a 0% base in the US context.
validity_reason: Macroprudential governance frameworks and institutional inertia change slowly over multi-year horizons.
